newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UNHCR sets up task force on northern Iraq.
newsitem.headline: UNHCR sets up task force on northern Iraq.

text.p: The United Nations refugee agency said on Tuesday that it had set up an emergency "task force" to draw up contingency plans in case of a refugee exodus from Iraq.

Ron Redmond, spokesman for the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), also told a news briefing that UNHCR staff in the northern Iraqi city of Arbil and in Sulaymaniya had reported both towns were quiet on Tuesday.
"They have set up this task force just specifically to watch this unfolding situation in Iraq in case there are large-scale movements...So far, we see no evidence of that," Redmond said.

UNHCR staff in Arbil described the situation there as calm, with most of the Iraqi troops appearing to have withdrawn. Citizens were trying to go about their normal business but there was no water or electricity -- a potential health risk.

"As of last night, the Iraqi flag was still flying over the former Kurdish parliament building (in Arbil). The rest of the city, however, was under the KDP flags," Redmond said, referring to the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) guerrillas.
"So far there did not appear to be any reaction to the reported U.S. military activities, at least not in Arbil," Redmond said. "In Sulaymaniya, it is quiet as far as we know."
